subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Penile and adrenal cancers: viral aetiology, lymph node dissection and adrenocortical management

steps.tx: Epithelial penile malignancy arises via two distinct pathogeneses. Up to 50% of **penile squamous cell carcinoma** cases are driven by high-risk **human papillomavirus** infections, predominantly genotypes 16 and 18, characterized by diffuse p16INK4a overexpression. Non-HPV-related carcinomas arise against a background of chronic foreskin inflammation, lichen sclerosus, and phimosis, demonstrating frequent somatic mutations in TP53 and NOTCH1.
steps.say: Epithelial penile malignancy arises via two distinct pathogeneses. right.title: Non-HPV Penile Carcinoma
points: Associated with phimosis and lichen sclerosus
Frequent TP53 mutations and poorer prognosis

steps.tx: Lymphatic dissemination in penile carcinoma follows an orderly anatomic hierarchy without skip lesions. Tumour emboli drain first to superficial inguinal nodes, then deep inguinal nodes, and finally external iliac pelvic nodes. Regional nodal metastasis is the single strongest determinant of disease-specific survival; bilateral **inguinal lymph node dissection** provides critical diagnostic staging and curative cytoreduction in men with intermediate-risk or high-risk invasive primary tumours.
steps.say: Lymphatic dissemination in penile carcinoma follows an orderly anatomic hierarchy without skip lesions. Tumour emboli drain first to superficial inguinal nodes, then deep inguinal nodes, and finally pelvic nodes. Nodal metastasis is the strongest determinant of survival; bilateral inguinal lymph node dissection provides critical staging and curative cytoreduction in invasive tumours.

steps.tx: Locally advanced fixed or bulky nodal metastases require multimodality downstaging. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy utilizing the **TIP regimen** combines paclitaxel, **ifosfamide**, and **cisplatin**. Administered for 4 cycles prior to planned surgical consolidation, TIP neoadjuvant chemotherapy achieves objective response rates of 50% to 55%, converting unresectable, fixed inguinal adenopathy into completely resectable surgical specimens and dramatically improving long-term overall survival.

steps.tx: Adrenocortical carcinoma is a highly aggressive endocrine malignancy presenting with hormone excess or abdominal mass effects. Functional hormonal hypersecretion occurs in over 60% of cases, commonly manifesting as rapid-onset **Cushing syndrome** from autonomous glucocorticoid release or virilisation from excessive adrenal androgen synthesis, characterized by elevated dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate DHEAS and 17-hydroxyprogesterone requiring formal endocrine biochemical workup.

right.title: Non-Functional Presentations
points: Flank pain, fullness, and early satiety

steps.tx: Pathological distinction between benign adrenocortical adenomas and invasive carcinomas requires multiparameter scoring. The **Weiss score** evaluates nine distinct microscopic criteria, including high mitotic rate exceeding 5 per 50 high-power fields, atypical mitotic figures, venous invasion, sinusoidal invasion, capsular invasion, low clear cell architecture under 25%, necrosis, and nuclear pleomorphism. A Weiss score of **3 or greater** establishes the definitive histological diagnosis of adrenocortical carcinoma.

steps.tx: Adjuvant medical therapy following complete surgical resection aims to prevent locoregional and distant recurrence. **Mitotane** o,p-DDD is an oral adrenolytic agent that selectively destroys adrenocortical cells by inhibiting mitochondrial sterol synthesis enzymes. In high-risk stage III disease or Weiss score greater than 6, adjuvant mitotane therapy for at least 2 years significantly prolongs recurrence-free survival, requiring structured monitoring to maintain therapeutic serum levels between **14 and 20 mg/L**.

Mitotane is an oral adrenolytic agent that selectively destroys adrenocortical cells by inhibiting mitochondrial enzymes. In high-risk disease, adjuvant mitotane therapy for at least 2 years prolongs recurrence-free survival, maintaining serum levels between 14 and 20 mg/L.

steps.tx: Metastatic or unresectable adrenocortical carcinoma mandates intensive combination systemic chemo-adrenolytic therapy. In the randomized international **FIRM-ACT trial**, the **EDP-M regimen** combining etoposide, doxorubicin, and cisplatin paired with oral mitotane demonstrated statistically superior response rates and progression-free survival compared to streptozocin plus mitotane. Concomitant high-dose hydrocortisone replacement is essential because mitotane induces CYP3A4, markedly accelerating steroid clearance.

right.title: Supportive Endocrinology Care
points: Monitor free urinary cortisol and ACTH levels

steps.tx: Pediatric and young adult adrenocortical carcinomas frequently occur as index presentations of hereditary syndromes. Germline **TP53 mutations** underlying **Li-Fraumeni syndrome** account for over 50% of pediatric adrenocortical tumours globally and more than 90% in southern Brazil due to the founder R337H mutation. Additional hereditary drivers include Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome with 11p15 uniparental disomy and Lynch syndrome, mandating comprehensive germline genetic counseling.
